observation_method.web: Pages were read through the agent's WebFetch tool, which converts a page to markdown and answers a prompt with a small model. Quotations below are as returned by that tool. No page bytes were stored locally, so no SHA-256 exists for the web observations. No page was copied wholesale.
observation_method.local: Local files were read and hashed by the agent.
observation_method.pending_live_hash: The live schema probe fetches README.md at the pinned revision and records its byte count and SHA-256 in its receipt. That hash is the byte-level binding for the dataset card.

sources.title: Essential-Web v1.0 dataset card (README.md at the pinned revision)
facts: YAML front matter declares license: odc-by.
"Essential-Web-v1.0 contributions are made available under the ODC attribution license" (linked to the ODC-By 1.0 text).
"users should also abide by the Common Crawl - Terms of Use".
"We do not alter the license of any of the underlying data."
DCLM pool: 89 resiliparse-extracted Common Crawl WARC snapshots, CC-MAIN-2013-20 to CC-MAIN-2022-49.
12 additional snapshots, CC-MAIN-2023-06 to CC-MAIN-2024-38; 101 Common Crawl snapshots processed.
Hash-based deduplication across all 101 snapshots; MinHash LSH deduplication (Jaccard threshold 0.7 as returned by the tool).
Quality filtering retaining English documents; every document classified with EAI-Taxonomy-0.5b.
The card states nothing about benchmark decontamination, evaluation-set removal, or removal of personal information.
sources.reviewer_conclusion: Matches the operator-provided facts. The card licenses Essential AI's contributions and explicitly does not relicense underlying web content.

sources.title: Common Crawl Terms of Use (page states last updated March 7, 2024)
facts: Crawled content "may be subject to separate terms of use or terms of service from the owners of such Crawled Content".
"BY USING THE CRAWLED CONTENT, YOU AGREE TO RESPECT THE COPYRIGHTS AND OTHER APPLICABLE RIGHTS OF THIRD PARTIES".
The tool found no attribution requirement on this page.
The terms include a user indemnification covering use of crawled content for developing, training or deploying AI systems.
sources.reviewer_conclusion: Common Crawl grants no rights in the underlying pages; third-party rights stay with their owners and the user carries that responsibility. The operator should read the full terms; this summary is not a substitute.
